about.text: The liquid left in the churn when cream turns to butter: thin and low in fat, with most of the cream's other milk solids still in it. Sold sweet, or soured with a culture as buttermilk; in Germany buttermilk may have no more than 1 % fat.

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: Same step as butter: the churn splits the cream into fat grains and this thin liquid, which keeps most of the cream's milk solids and the membrane material of the fat globules.

facts.v: About 0.5 %; fat lost to buttermilk 0.5–1.2 % of cream fat in a small-churn study
Fat left in buttermilk as share of cream fat; below 0.70 is acceptable
Sweet cream buttermilk has a much higher pH than sour cream buttermilk; rich in fat-globule membrane
